177.subject: Botany
177.text:
Which of the following organelles contain DNA?
(i) Mitochondria (ii) Chloroplasts (iii) Golgi bodies (iv) Ribosomes
177.sol: Both mitochondria and chloroplast are semi-autonomous organelles as they possess their own DNA, RNA and 70 S ribosomes to have sufficient functional independence from cellular machinery. Chloroplasts DNA is bigger than mitochondrial DNA. However, genetic information contained in these DNAs is limited. DNA is naked (without histone proteins) in both.

On comparing with $9 x+y-28=0$, we get

\Rightarrow & h²+k²-2 h+4 k-20=4 h²+4 k²-8 h-32 k+4 \\
\Rightarrow & 3 h²+3 k²-6 h-36 k+24=0 \\

7425.text: Let A  $\left(3 - i\right)$, B   $\left(2 + i\right)$ be two points in the Argand plane. If the point $P$ represents the complex number $z = x + iy,$ which satisfies $\left| z - 3 + i\right| = \left| z - 2 - i\right|,$ then the locus of the point $P$ is

7425.sol:
Given,

$A\left(3 - i\right) ⇒ A ≡ \left(3, - 1\right)$

$B\left(2 + i\right) ⇒ B ≡ \left(2, 1\right)$

Now,

$\left|z - 3 + i\right| = \left|z - 2 - i\right|$

$⇒ \left|z - \left(3 - i\right)\right| = \left|z - \left(2 + i\right)\right| ≡ \left\{\left|z - A\right| = \left|z - B\right|\right\}$

$⇒ \left|z - \left(3 - i\right)\right| = \left|z - \left(2 + i\right)\right| ≡ \left\{\left|P - A\right| = \left|P - B\right|\right\}$

Therefore, we get $AP = BP$.

Point $P$ is moving along the line $CM$ such that $AP = BP$.

Hence, locus of the point $P$ is the perpendicular bisector of line $AB$.

9659.subject: Mathematics
9659.text: Let $f: R^{+} \to R^{+}$ be a function satisfying $f\left(x\right) - x = \lambda$ (constant), $∀ x \in \mathbbR^{+}$ and $f\left(xf\left(y\right)\right) = f\left(xy\right) + x, ∀ x, y, \in \mathbbR^{+}.$ Then $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(f\left(x\right)\right)\dfrac{1}{3} - 1}{\left(f\left(x\right)\right)\dfrac{1}{2} - 1} =$
9659.sol:
Given relation is $f\left(x . f\left(y\right)\right) = f\left(xy\right) + x . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Interchanging $x$ and y in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$f\left(y . f\left(x\right)\right) = f\left(yx\right) + y . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Again replacing $x$ with $f\left(x\right)$ in equation $\left(2\right)$ we get

$f\left(f\left(x\right) \cdot f\left(y\right)\right) = f\left(y \cdot f\left(x\right)\right) + f\left(x\right)$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(x\right) \cdot f\left(y\right)\right) = f\left(yx\right) + y + f\left(x\right) . . . \left(3\right)$ {from equation $2$}

Again interchanging $x$ and $y$ in equation $\left(3\right)$, we have

$f\left(f\left(y\right) \cdot f\left(x\right)\right) = f\left(yx\right) + x + f\left(y\right) . . . . . . . \left(4\right)$

Now from equation $\left(3\right) \text{ and } \left(4\right)$ we get,

$f\left(xy\right) + y + f\left(x\right) = f\left(yx\right) + x + f\left(y\right) . . . . . . \left(5\right)$

Suppose $f\left(x\right) - x = f\left(y\right) - y = \lambda$

Substituting $f\left(x\right) = \lambda + x$ in equation $\left(5\right)$ we have

$x \cdot f\left(y\right) + \lambda = \left(xy + \lambda\right) + x$

$⇒ x \cdot f\left(y\right) = xy + x$

Therefore $x\left(y + \lambda\right) = xy + x\left[∵ f\left(y\right) = \lambda + y\right]$

$⇒ \lambda = x ⇒ \lambda = 1\left(∵ x > 0\right)$

So $f\left(x\right) = x + \lambda = x + 1$

Hence $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}{{\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{2}} - 1} = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{3}} - 1}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{2}} - 1}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{3}} - 1}{1 + x - 1}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{1 + x - 1}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{2}} - 1}\right)$$= \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

If \($\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{[(a-n) n x-\tan x] \sin n x}{x^2}=$0,(n  ≠ 0)\)
then the minimum possible positive value of \(a\) is
9693.sol:
\begin{aligned}& $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{((a-n) n x-\tan x) \sin n x}{x^2}=$0, n ≠ 0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{(a-n) n x}{x}-\frac{\tan x}{x}\right) \frac{\sin (n x)}{x}=$0 \\
& \$quad\left[\because \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin n x}{n x}=$n\right] \\
& \Rightarrow \quad $n\left($a n-n²-1\right)=0 \Rightarrow \quad $a=n+\frac{1}{n},$n ≠ 0 \\
& \because \quad $\frac{n+\frac{1}{n}}{2} \geq \sqrt{n \frac{1}{n}} \text{ (by AM } \geq \text{ GM) }$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{a}{2} \geq$1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad a \geq 2
\end{aligned}\)
\(\therefore\) Minimum possible positive value$ of \(a\) is 2. Hence, option (c) is correct.

9994.text: Suppose $A$ and $B$ are the points at which the line $x+y-\lambda=0$ meets the pair of straight lines $x^2+y^2-2 x-4 y+2=0$. If $\angle A O B=90^{{}^{\circ}}$, then a value of $\lambda$ is
9994.sol:
Given, line is $x+y-\lambda=0\Rightarrow \quad x+y=\lambda\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x+y}{\lambda}=1$...(i)
and pair of straight lines is
$x^2+y^2-2 x-4 y+2=0$
We will make homogeneous of the above line.
$x^2+y^2-2 x(\mathrm{l})-4 y(\mathrm{l})+2(\mathrm{l})^2=0\Rightarrow \quad x^2+y^2-2 x\left(\frac{x+y}{\lambda}\right)-4 y\left(\frac{x+y}{\lambda}\right)+2\left(\frac{x+y}{\lambda}\right)^2=0 \quad$ [using Eq. (i)]
$\Rightarrow \lambda^2\left(x^2+y^2\right)-2 x^2 \lambda-2 y x \lambda-4 x y \lambda-4 y^2 \lambda+2\left(x^2+y^2+2 x y\right)=0\Rightarrow\left(\lambda^2-2 \lambda+2\right) x^2+(4 x y-6 x y \lambda)\left(\lambda^2-4 \lambda+2\right) y^2=0\Rightarrow\left(\lambda^2-2 \lambda+2\right) x^2+(4-6 \lambda) x y+\left(\lambda^2-4 \lambda+2\right) y^2=0$
Now, $\angle A O B=90^{{}^{\circ}}$ where $O$ is the origin.
Condition for $\angle A D B=90^{{}^{\circ}}$ is given by;
$\left(\right.$ Coefficient of $\left.x^2\right)+\left(\right.$ Coefficient of $\left.y^2\right)=0\Rightarrow \quad\left(\lambda^2-2 \lambda+2\right)+\left(\lambda^2-4 \lambda+2\right)=02 \lambda^2-6 \lambda+4=0\Rightarrow \quad \lambda^2-3 \lambda+2=0\Rightarrow \quad(\lambda-1)(\lambda-2)=0\Rightarrow \quad \lambda=1,2$
Hence, option (a) is correct.

10844.text: Given that the probability of a man hitting a target with a gun is $\frac{1}{3}. If he fires 8 times, then the probability of his hitting the target atleast twice is$
10844.sol:
Probability to hit the target $=\frac{1}{3}$ Probability to not hit the target $=1-\frac{1}{3}=\frac{2}{3}$
Probability to hit the target atleast twice is $\begin{aligned}& =P(2)+P(3)+P(4)+\ldots+P(8) \\
& =1-[P(0)+P(1)] \\
& =1-\left[\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^8+{ }^8C_1 \cdot\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^7 \cdot \frac{1}{3}\right]\\
& =1-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^7 \cdot \left[\frac{2}{3}+8 \cdot \frac{1}{3}\right]\\
& =1-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^7 \cdot \frac{10}{3}=1-5 \cdot\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^8
\end{aligned}$

11076.text: What is the greatest angle of the triangle whose sides are $x^2+x+1,2 x+1, x^2-1$ ?
11076.sol:
Sides of triangle are
$\begin{aligned} & x^2+x+1,2 x+1 \text{$ and $} x^2-1 \\ & x^2+x+1 \text{ is the greatest side. }\end{aligned}\therefore \cos A=\frac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2 b c}$
Here, $a=x^2+x+1, b=2 x+1, c=x^2-1\therefore \cos A=\frac{(2 x+1)^2+\left(x^2-1\right)^2-\left(x^2+x+1\right)^2}{2(2 x+1)\left(x^2-1\right)}\Rightarrow \cos A=\frac{\left.(2 x+1)^2+(x^2-1+x^2+x+1(x^2-1-x^2-x-1\right)}{2(2 x+1)\left(x^2-1\right)}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \cos A=\frac{(2 x+1)^2+\left(2 x^2+x\right)(-x-2)}{2(2 x+1)\left(x^2-1\right)} \\ & \Rightarrow \cos A=\frac{(2 x+1)\left(2 x+1-x^2-2 x\right)}{2(2 x+1)\left(x^2-1\right)}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \cos A=\frac{-(2 x+1)\left(x^2-1\right)}{2(2 x+1)\left(x^2-1\right)}=\frac{-1}{2}\therefore \quad A=120^{{}^{\circ}}$

21080.subject: Mathematics
21080.text: If the sum of the coefficients of the first three terms in the expansion of $\left(x-\dfrac{a}{x^2}\right)^{12}, x \neq 0$ is 559. Find the value of '$a$' if '$a$' belongs to positive integers
21080.sol:
The expansion of $\left(x - \dfrac{a}{x^2}\right)^{12}$ is given by the binomial theorem as $\sum_{r=0}^{12} {^{12}C_{r}} (x)^{12-r} \left(-\dfrac{a}{x^2}\right)^{r}$.

The first three terms correspond to $r=0, 1, 2$.

For $r=0$: Term is ${^{12}C_{0}} (x)^{12} (-a)^{0} (x)^{-0} = 1 \cdot x^{12}$. The coefficient is $1$.

For $r=1$: Term is ${^{12}C_{1}} (x)^{11} (-a)^{1} (x)^{-2} = 12 \cdot (-a) \cdot x^{9} = -12a x^{9}$. The coefficient is $-12a$.

For $r=2$: Term is ${^{12}C_{2}} (x)^{10} (-a)^{2} (x)^{-4} = 66 \cdot a^{2} \cdot x^{6} = 66a^{2} x^{6}$. The coefficient is $66a^{2}$.

The sum of these coefficients is given as $559$.

$1 - 12a + 66a^{2} = 559$

$66a^{2} - 12a - 558 = 0$

Dividing by $6$: $11a^{2} - 2a - 93 = 0$.

Solving the quadratic equation using the quadratic formula $a = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^{2} - 4ac}}{2a}$:

$a = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 4(11)(-93)}}{22} = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 + 4092}}{22} = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{4096}}{22} = \dfrac{2 \pm 64}{22}$.

Since $a$ is a positive integer, $a = \dfrac{2 + 64}{22} = \dfrac{66}{22} = 3$.

Answer: 3

21181.subject: Mathematics
21181.sol:
Let $z = \dfrac{1 - i\sqrt{3}}{1 + i\sqrt{3}}$.

Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator, $1 - i\sqrt{3}$:

$z = \dfrac{(1 - i\sqrt{3})(1 - i\sqrt{3})}{(1 + i\sqrt{3})(1 - i\sqrt{3})}$

$z = \dfrac{1 - 2i\sqrt{3} + (i\sqrt{3})^2}{1^2 + (\sqrt{3})^2}$

$z = \dfrac{1 - 2i\sqrt{3} - 3}{1 + 3}$

$z = \dfrac{-2 - 2i\sqrt{3}}{4}$

$z = -\dfrac{1}{2} - i\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

The complex number $z$ is in the third quadrant since both the real part $x = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ and the imaginary part $y = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ are negative.

The argument $\theta$ is given by $\theta = -\pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\left|\dfrac{y}{x}\right|\right)$ or simply by observing the angle in the third quadrant.

$\tan(\alpha) = \left|\dfrac{-\sqrt{3}/2}{-1/2}\right| = \sqrt{3} \Rightarrow \alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

Since the point lies in the third quadrant, the argument is $-\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = -\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{-2 \pi}{3}$

21509.subject: Mathematics
21509.sol:
Given integral is $I = \int \dfrac{e^{\log\left(1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)}}{x^2 + \dfrac{1}{x^2}}\ dx$

Using the property $e^{\log f(x)} = f(x)$, the integral simplifies to:

$I = \int \dfrac{1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}}{x^2 + \dfrac{1}{x^2}}\ dx$

The denominator can be rewritten by completing the square:

$x^2 + \dfrac{1}{x^2} = \left(x - \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^2 + 2$

So the integral becomes:

$I = \int \dfrac{1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}}{\left(x - \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^2 + 2}\ dx$

Let $x - \dfrac{1}{x} = t$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get:

$\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x^2}\right) dx = dt$

Substituting this into the integral:

$I = \int \dfrac{dt}{t^2 + (\sqrt{2})^2}$

Using the standard integral formula $\int \dfrac{dx}{x^2 + a^2} = \dfrac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right) + C$:

$I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{t}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + C$

Substituting back $t = x - \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{x^2-1}{x}$:

$I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x^2-1}{\sqrt{2}\,x}\right) + C$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x^2-1}{\sqrt{2}\,x}\right) + C$

21894.subject: Mathematics
21894.text: In an entrance test, there are multiple choice questions. There are four possible answers to each question of which only one is correct. The probability that a student knows the answer to a question is $90 \%$. If he gets the correct answer to a question, then the probability that he was guessing is
21894.sol:
Let $K$ be the event that the student knows the answer and $G$ be the event that the student guesses the answer. Let $C$ be the event that the student gets the correct answer.

Given $P(K) = 0.9$ and $P(G) = 1 - 0.9 = 0.1$.

If the student knows the answer, the probability of getting it correct is $P(C|K) = 1$.

If the student guesses, there are 4 options and only 1 is correct, so the probability of getting it correct is $P(C|G) = \dfrac{1}{4} = 0.25$.

The total probability of getting the correct answer is $P(C) = P(C|K)P(K) + P(C|G)P(G) = (1)(0.9) + (0.25)(0.1) = 0.9 + 0.025 = 0.925$.

We need to find the probability that the student was guessing given that he got the correct answer, which is $P(G|C)$.

Using Bayes' Theorem, $P(G|C) = \dfrac{P(C|G)P(G)}{P(C)} = \dfrac{0.25 \times 0.1}{0.925} = \dfrac{0.025}{0.925} = \dfrac{25}{925} = \dfrac{1}{37}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{37}$

Given $\cos \theta = \dfrac{1}{2} \left($x + $\dfrac{1}{x}\right), we have $x + $\dfrac{1}{x} =$2 \cos $\theta.

Squaring both sides:

\left($x + $\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^$2 = (2 \cos $\theta)^$2$

$x^2 + $\dfrac{1}{x^2} +$2 = 4 \cos^2 $\theta

$x^2 + $\dfrac{1}{x^2} =$4 \cos^2 $\theta -$2$

Now, we need to find \dfrac{1}{2} \left($x^2 + $\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right):

\dfrac{1}{2}\left($x^2 + $\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}($4 \cos^2 $\theta -$2) = 2 \cos^2 $\theta -$1$.

Using the identity $\sin^2 $\theta + \cos^2 \theta =$1$, we can write $1 = \sin^2 $\theta + \cos^2 \theta.

Substituting this into the expression:

$2 \cos^2 $\theta - (\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta) = \cos^2 \theta - \sin^2 \theta.

Answer: $\cos ^2 $\theta-\sin ^$2 $\theta$

23268.text: In a nuclear fusion reaction, two nuclei, $A$ and $B$ fuse to produce a nucleus $C$, releasing an amount of energy $\Delta \mathrm{E}$ in the process. If the mass defects of the three nuclei are $\Delta M_A, \Delta M_B$ and $\Delta M_C$ respectively, then which of the following relations is true? (c$ is the speed of light).$
23268.sol:
Energy released in fusion: $\Delta E = BE_C - (BE_A + BE_B)$

Since $BE = \Delta M \cdot c^2$:

$\Delta E = (\Delta M_C)c^2 - [(\Delta M_A)c^2 + (\Delta M_B)c^2]$

Dividing by $c^2$:

$\dfrac{\Delta E}{c^2} = \Delta M_C - \Delta M_A - \Delta M_B$

$\Delta M_A + \Delta M_B = \Delta M_C - \dfrac{\Delta E}{c^2}$

23281.subject: Physics
23281.text: The mass density of a nucleus varies with mass number $A$ as
23281.sol:
The radius of a nucleus is given by the relation $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, where $R_0$ is a constant and $A$ is the mass number.

The volume of the nucleus is $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi (R_0 A^{1/3})^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3 A$.

The mass of the nucleus is approximately $M = A \times m_p$, where $m_p$ is the mass of a nucleon.

The mass density $\rho$ is given by $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V} = \dfrac{A m_p}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3 A} = \dfrac{m_p}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3}$.

Since $m_p$, $R_0$, and $\pi$ are constants, the density $\rho$ is independent of the mass number $A$. Therefore, the density varies as $A^0$.

Answer: $\mathop A\limits^o $

25828.text: Let $AP\left(a; d\right)$ denote the set of all the terms of an infinite arithmetic progression with first term a and common difference $d > 0 .$ If $AP\left(1; 3\right) ∩ AP\left(2; 5\right) ∩ AP\left(3; 7\right) = AP\left(a; d\right)$ then $a + d$ equals ____
25828.sol:
Let ${T}_{\left(1, m\right)}: {m}^{th}$ term of ${1}^{st}$ series $A\left(1; 3\right)$
${T}_{\left(2, n\right)}: {n}^{th}$ term of ${2}^{nd}$ series $A\left(2; 5\right)$
${T}_{\left(3, r\right)}: {r}^{th}$ term of ${3}^{rd}$ series $A ( 3; 7 )$
For common terms
${T}_{( 1, m )} = {T}_{( 2, n )} = {T}_{( 3, r )}$
$1 + 3\left(m - 1\right) = 2 + 5\left(n - 1\right) = 3 + 7\left(r - 1\right)$
$3m - 2 = 5n - 3 = 7r - 4$
$⇒ m = \dfrac{5n - 1}{3}andr = \dfrac{5n + 1}{7}$
For $‘m’$ to be a natural number $n = 2,5, 11, \ldots$
And for $‘r’$ to be a natural number $n = 4,11, \ldots$
When $n = 11, m = 18 and r = 8$
$⇒$ For ${1}^{st}$ common term of three series $A ( a, d )$
$a = {1}^{st}$ term of $A ( 1,3 )$
$a = 1 + ( 181 ) 3 = 52$
$⇒$ Common difference of $A\left(a, d\right) = LCM$ of common difference of $\left(A\left(1; 3\right), A\left(2; 5\right), A\left(3; 7\right)\right)$
$d = LCM ( 3, 5, 7 )$
$d = 105$
Hence, $a + d = 52 + 105 = 157$

the process during the path $A \rightarrow B$ is isothermal

heat flows out of the gas during the path $B \rightarrow C \rightarrow D$

work done during the path $A \rightarrow B \rightarrow C$ is zero

positive work is done by the gas in the cycle $A B C D A$.
26702.sol:
(A) $p-V$ graph is not rectangular hyperbola. Therefore, process $A-B$ is not isothermal.
(B) In process $B C D$, product of $p V$ (therefore temperature and intemal energy) is decreasing. Further, volume is decreasing. Hence, work done is also negative. Hence, $Q$ will be negative or heat will flow out of the gas.
(C) $W_{A B C}=$ positive
(D) For clockwise cycle on $p-V$ diagram with $P$ on $y$-axis, net work done is positive.

28541.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The decrease in first ionization enthalpy from $B$ to $Al$ is much larger than that from $Al$ to $Ga$.

Statement II: The d orbitals in $Ga$ are completely filled.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
Both the statements I and II are correct
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Both the statements I and II are incorrect
28541.sol:
First ionization enthalpy (IE1) of B, Al, Ga are 801, 577 and 579 kJ/mol respectively.

As decrease in first ionization enthalpy is much larger from B to Al. $∆ {IE}_{1}$ of B and Al is greater than $∆ {IE}_{1}$ of Al and Ga. So, the statement I is correct.

This is due to completely filled d-orbitals in Ga and d-electron have low screening effect to compensate the increase in nuclear charge. So, The statement II is also correct.

Hence, the correct option is B.

Match List I with List II:

List I
(Complexes)		 List II
(Hybridisation)
(A) $\left[Ni ( CO{)}_{4}\right]$ I ${sp}^{3}$
(B) ${\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}$ II ${dsp}^{2}$
(C) ${\left[Fe{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +}$ III ${sp}^{3}{d}^{2}$
(D) ${\left[Fe{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +}$ IV ${d}^{2}{sp}^{3}$
options: A – II, B – I, C – III, D – IV
A – I, B – II, C – III, D – IV
A – II, B – I, C – IV, D – III
A – I, B– II, C – IV, D – III
28799.sol:
$Ni$ is in zero oxidation state in $[ Ni ( CO{)}_{4} ]$. So, the electronic configuration of $Ni$ is $3{d}^{8}4{s}^{2}$. As $CO$ is a strong ligand, it pushes all the electrons in the 3d orbital, therefore the hybridisation of $[ Ni ( CO{)}_{4} ]$ is sp3 and it has tetrahedral geometry. It is diamagnetic due to the absence of unpaired electrons.

${\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}$ ion, oxidation state of $Cu$ is +2 and its valence shell electronic configuration is $3{d}^{9}$. So, there would be a rearrangement of electrons in ${Cu}^{2 +}$ because of the ${NH}_{3}$ strong field ligand . And the last electron in the d-orbital would be out waiting for the N's electrons to fill up first. So, the 4 electron pairs from $N$ would be in one 3d, one 4s, & two 4p orbitals and in the third place of 4p orbital, the e- from 3d would take place. So, you can say the hybridisation here would be ${dsp}^{2}$.

${\left[Fe{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +}$ ion, oxidation state of $Fe$ is +2 and its valence shell electronic configuration is $3{d}^{6}$. ${NH}_{3}$ is strong field ligand with complex. So, no pairing will be there. So, you can say the hybridisation here would be ${d}^{2}{sp}^{3}$.

${\left[Fe{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +}$ ion, oxidation state of $Fe$ is +2 and its valence shell electronic configuration is $3{d}^{6}$. There are 4 unpaired electrons in 3d orbital. So, you can say the hybridisation here would be ${sp}^{3}{d}^{2}$.

So, correct order of matching is given in the below table:

List I
(Complexes)		 List II
(Hybridisation)
$\left[Ni ( CO{)}_{4}\right]$ ${sp}^{3}$
${\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}$ ${dsp}^{2}$

33675.subject: Mathematics
33675.text: If a tangent to the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1$ intersects the coordinate axes at distinct points $P$ and $Q,$ then the locus of the mid-point of $PQ$ is:
33675.sol:
Any point on the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = {r}^{2}$ is $\left(rcos\theta, rsin\theta\right)$ and the equation of the tangent at this point is $xcos\theta + ysin\theta = r .$

Thus, any point on circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1$ is $\left(cos\theta, sin\theta\right)$ and the equation of tangent at this point is $xcos\theta + ysin\theta = 1 .$

To find the point where this line intersects the $x$-axis, put $y = 0,$$⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{cos\theta}$

$⇒ P = \left(\dfrac{1}{cos\theta}, 0\right)$

And, to find the point where this line intersects the $y$-axis, put $x = 0,$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{sin\theta}$

$⇒ Q = \left(0, \dfrac{1}{sin\theta}\right)$

The mid-point of a line segment joining the points $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ and $\left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)$ is $\left(\dfrac{{x}_{1} + {x}_{2}}{2}, \dfrac{{y}_{1} + {y}_{2}}{2}\right)$

Let, midpoint of $PQ$ is $\left(h, k\right)$

$∴ \left(h, k\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2cos\theta}, \dfrac{1}{2sin\theta}\right)$

$⇒ h = \dfrac{1}{2cos\theta} \text{ and } k = \dfrac{1}{2sin\theta}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2h} \text{ and } sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2k}$

$∵ \sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4{h}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{4{k}^{2}} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{{h}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{k}^{2}} = 4$

To get the locus of the required point, replace $\left(h, k\right)$ by $\left(x, y\right)$

$∴$Locus is $\dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{y}^{2}} = 4$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} – 4{x}^{2}{y}^{2} = 0 .$

34691.subject: Mathematics
34691.text: If $\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1 + x - {y}^{2}}{y}, x\left(1\right) = 1,$ then $5x\left(2\right)$ is equal to:
34691.sol:
Given: $\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1 + x - {y}^{2}}{y}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1 + x}{y} - y$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} - \dfrac{1 + x}{y} = - y$

Now let $1 + x = t ⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{dt}{dy}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dy} - \dfrac{t}{y} = - y$

$⇒ IF = {e}^{∫ - \dfrac{1}{y}dy}$

$⇒ IF = {e}^{- logy}$

$⇒ IF = {e}^{log\dfrac{1}{y}}$

$⇒ IF = \dfrac{1}{y}$

So, the solution of the given differential equation is

$\dfrac{t}{y} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{y} \times \left(- y\right)dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{y} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{y} \times \left(- y\right)dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{y} = - y + c$

Also, $x\left(1\right) = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{1} = - 1 + c$

$⇒ c = 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{y} = - y + 3$

Putting $y = 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{2} = - 2 + 3$

$⇒ \left(1 + x\right) = 2$

$⇒ x = 1$

$⇒ 5x = 5$

35054.subject: Mathematics
35054.text: If the tangent to the parabola ${y}^{2} = x$ at a point $\left(\alpha, \beta\right), \left(\beta > 0\right) is also a tangent$ to the ellipse,{x}^{2} + 2{y}^{2} = 1$ then $\alpha$ is equal to:$
35054.sol:
Since $\left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ lies on the parabola $⇒ \alpha = {\beta}^{2}$

$⇒ \left(\alpha, \beta\right) = \left({\beta}^{2}, \beta\right)$

Tangent to a parabola ${y}^{2} = 4ax$ at a point $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ is $y{y}_{1} = 2a\left(x + {x}_{1}\right)$

Therefore, tangent to the parabola ${y}^{2} = x$ at $\left({\beta}^{2}, \beta\right)$ is$y ⋅ \beta = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x + {\beta}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{x}{2\beta} + \dfrac{\beta}{2} . . . \left(i\right)$

Tangent to parabola is also a tangent to ellipse

${x}^{2} + 2{y}^{2} = 1 ⇒ {x}^{2} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = 1$

And, a line $y = mx + c$ is a tangent to the ellipse $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ if ${c}^{2} = {a}^{2}{m}^{2} + {b}^{2}$

Using the condition ${c}^{2} = {a}^{2}{m}^{2} + {b}^{2},$ we get

$\dfrac{{\beta}^{2}}{4} = {1}^{2}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2\beta}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\beta}^{2}}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4{\beta}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ {\beta}^{4} - 2{\beta}^{2} - 1 = 0$

Using Sridharacharya's Formula the roots of a quadratic equation $a{x}^{2} + bx + c = 0, a \ne 0$ are $x = \dfrac{- b \pm \sqrt{{b}^{2} - 4ac}}{2a}$

$⇒ {\beta}^{2} = \dfrac{- \left(- 2\right) \pm \sqrt{{\left(- 2\right)}^{2} - 4 \times 1 \times \left(- 1\right)}}{2 \times 1}$

$⇒ {\beta}^{2} = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{8}}{2}$

$⇒ {\beta}^{2} = 1 + \sqrt{2}$ or ${\beta}^{2} = 1 - \sqrt{2} ($Neglected as ${\beta}^{2}$ is positive$)$

$⇒ {\beta}^{2} = \sqrt{2} + 1$

$⇒ \alpha = \sqrt{2} + 1 .$

37026.subject: Mathematics
37026.text: Let $A$ be the set of first 101 terms of an A.P., whose first term is 1 and the common difference is 5 and let $B$ be the set of first 71 terms of an A.P., whose first term is 9 and the common difference is 7. Then the number of elements in $A \cap B$, which are divisible by 3, is :
37026.sol:
The set $A$ consists of the first 101 terms of an A.P. with first term $a_1 = 1$ and common difference $d_1 = 5$.

The terms of $A$ are $1, 6, 11, 16, \dots, 1 + (101-1) \times 5 = 501$.

The set $B$ consists of the first 71 terms of an A.P. with first term $b_1 = 9$ and common difference $d_2 = 7$.

The terms of $B$ are $9, 16, 23, 30, \dots, 9 + (71-1) \times 7 = 499$.

The first common term of $A$ and $B$ is $16$.

The common difference of the terms in $A \cap B$ is the least common multiple of $d_1$ and $d_2$, which is $\text{lcm}(5, 7) = 35$.

The general term of $A \cap B$ is given by $T_k = 16 + 35k$, where $k \ge 0$ is an integer.

Since the maximum possible value in $A \cap B$ cannot exceed the maximum value in $B$ (which is $499$), we have:

$16 + 35k \le 499$

$35k \le 483$

$k \le 13.8$

Thus, the possible values for $k$ are $0, 1, 2, \dots, 13$.

We require the terms in $A \cap B$ to be divisible by $3$. Therefore:

$16 + 35k \equiv 0 \pmod 3$

$1 + 2k \equiv 0 \pmod 3$

$2k \equiv 2 \pmod 3$

$k \equiv 1 \pmod 3$

The values of $k$ in the range $0 \le k \le 13$ that satisfy $k \equiv 1 \pmod 3$ are $1, 4, 7, 10, 13$.

There are exactly $5$ such values of $k$, which correspond to $5$ elements in $A \cap B$ that are divisible by $3$.

Answer: $5$

37665.text: Let ABC be an equilateral triangle with orthocenter at the origin and the side BC on the line $x+2 \sqrt{2} y=4$. If the co-ordinates of the vertex A are $(\alpha, \beta)$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to $|\alpha+\sqrt{2} \beta|$ is
37665.sol:
Let ABC be an equilateral triangle with orthocenter at the origin O(0,0) and side BC on the line $x + 2\sqrt{2}y = 4$.
Since $m_{BC} \cdot m_{AD} = -1$:
$\left(-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)\left(\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\right) = -1 \Rightarrow \beta = 2\sqrt{2}\alpha$ ...(1)
Distance from O to BC: $OD = \frac{|-4|}{\sqrt{1+8}} = \frac{4}{3}$
For equilateral triangle: $AO = \frac{8}{3}$, so $AD = \frac{4}{3} + \frac{8}{3} = 4$
$\frac{|\alpha + 2\sqrt{2}\beta - 4|}{3} = 4 \Rightarrow \alpha = \frac{16}{9}$ or $-\frac{8}{9}$
Since A(\alpha, \beta)$ and O(0,0) lie on the same side of BC (origin gives $0+0-4 < 0$), we need $\alpha + 2\sqrt{2}\beta - 4 < 0$.
$(\alpha, \beta) = $\left(-\frac{8}{9}, -\frac{16\sqrt{2}}{9}\right)$
$\lfloor |\alpha + \sqrt{2}\beta| \rfloor = \left\lfloor \left|\frac{-8-32}{9}\right| \right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{40}{9} \right\rfloor = 4$

38834.subject: Physics
38834.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I: The reactance of an ac circuit is zero. It is possible that the circuit contains a capacitor and an inductor.
Statement-II: In ac circuit, the average power delivered by the source never becomes zero.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
38834.sol:
The reactance of a circuit containing a capacitor and an inductor is given by $X = {X}_{L} - {X}_{C} = \omegaL - \dfrac{1}{\omegaC}$. An AC circuit has zero reactance at resonance, i.e., when, ${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$. So, first statement is true.

The power consumption in an AC circuit is zero when circuit contains only inductance or capacitance since average power consumed in a cycle is zero for inductance or capacitance. So, second statement is false.

39149.text:
Two parallel plate capacitors ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ each having capacitance of $10\mu F$ are individually charged by a $100V$ D.C. source. Capacitor ${C}_{1}$ is kept connected to the source and a dielectric slab is inserted between it plates. Capacitor ${C}_{2}$ is disconnected from the source and then a dielectric slab is inserted in it. Afterwards the capacitor ${C}_{1}$ is also disconnected from the source and the two capacitors are finally connected in parallel combination. The common potential of the combination will be _____ $V$.

(Assuming Dielectric constant $= 10$)
39149.sol:
As source is connected in the process therefore, additional charge will be provided. Therefore, charge on ${C}_{1} = K\left(CV\right)$.

Since source is disconnected, so its charge will remain the same. Then, charge on ${C}_{2} = CV$.

New capacitance in both cases will become, $KC$.

When they are connected in parallel charge will be equally divided so charge on one capacitor is $q = \left(\dfrac{K + 1}{2}\right)CV$.

So common potential,

${V}^{'} = \dfrac{q}{KC} = \dfrac{K + 1}{2K}V = 55V$.

For loop containing voltmeter and $10Ω$ resistor, $1 . 2 - 10i = 0 ⇒ i = 0 . 12A$.

Reading of voltmeter should be,

$1 . 2 = 1 . 5 - i\left(\dfrac{r}{2}\right) ⇒ i\left(\dfrac{r}{2}\right) = 0 . 3 ⇒ r = \dfrac{0 . 6}{i} = \dfrac{0 . 6}{0 . 12} = 5Ω$

Average induced EMF is given by, $ε = N\left(\dfrac{∆ ϕ}{t}\right)$

Also, change in flux $∆ ϕ = ( ∆ B ) A$

Given: ${B}_{i} = 5000T$,

${B}_{f} = 3000T$

$d = 0 . 02m ⇒ r = \dfrac{d}{2} = 0 . 01m$

$∆ ϕ = ( ∆ B ) A$

40810.subject: Physics
40810.text: If a body of mass $1$ kg falls on the earth from infinity, it attains velocity $(v)$ and kinetic energy $(k)$ on reaching the surface of earth. The values of $v$ and $k$ respectively are _______. (Take radius of earth to be $6400$ km and $g = 9.8$ m/s$^2$)
40810.sol:
By conservation of mechanical energy, the total energy of the body at infinity is zero.

When the body reaches the surface of the earth, its potential energy is $-\dfrac{GMm}{R}$ and kinetic energy is $k = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$.

$0 = k - \dfrac{GMm}{R}$

$k = \dfrac{GMm}{R} = mgR$

Substituting $m = 1$ kg, $g = 9.8$ m/s$^2$, and $R = 6400 \times 10^3$ m:

$k = 1 \times 9.8 \times 6400 \times 10^3 = 6.272 \times 10^7$ J

The velocity $v$ is given by $\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = k$.

$v = \sqrt{2gR} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 6400 \times 10^3}$

$v = \sqrt{125.44 \times 10^6} = 11.2 \times 10^3$ m/s $= 11.2$ km/s

Answer: $11.2$ km/s; $6.27 \times 10^7$ J

40895.text: A body of mass $m$ is projected with velocity $\lambda{v}_{e}$ in vertically upward direction from the surface of the earth into space. It is given that ${v}_{e}$ is escape velocity and $\lambda < 1$. If air resistance is considered to the negligible, then the maximum height from the centre of earth, to which the body can go, will be ($R$ : radius of earth)
40895.sol:
Escape velocity is given by, ${v}_{e} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2G{M}_{e}}{{R}_{e}}}$

If the body goes to the height $h$ from the surface of the earth, using mechanical energy conservation,

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}m{\left(\lambda\sqrt{\dfrac{2G{M}_{e}}{{R}_{e}}}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{{R}_{e}} = - \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{{R}_{e} + h}$

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2}\dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{{R}_{e}} - \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{{R}_{e}} = - \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{{R}_{e} + h}$

$⇒ \left({R}_{e} + h\right) = \dfrac{{R}_{e}}{1 - {\lambda}^{2}}$

43424.subject: Physics
43424.text: Refer to the logic circuit given below. For two inputs $(A=1, B=1)$ and $(A=0, B=1)$, output $(Y)$ will be __________.
43424.sol:
From the given logic circuit, we can determine the Boolean expression for the output $Y$.

The output of the NOT gate is $\bar{A}$.

The inputs to the OR gate are $\bar{A}$ and $B$, so its output is $\bar{A} + B$.

The inputs to the AND gate are $\bar{A}$ and $B$, so its output is $\bar{A} \cdot B$.

These two outputs are fed into a NOR gate. The final output $Y$ is given by:

$Y = \overline{(\bar{A} + B) + (\bar{A} \cdot B)}$

Simplifying the Boolean expression:

$Y = \overline{\bar{A} + B + \bar{A}B}$

$Y = \overline{\bar{A} + B(1 + \bar{A})}$

$Y = \overline{\bar{A} + B}$

Using De Morgan's laws:

$Y = \overline{\bar{A}} \cdot \bar{B} = A \cdot \bar{B}$

Now, we evaluate $Y$ for the given input combinations:

For $A = 1, B = 1$:

$Y = 1 \cdot \bar{1} = 1 \cdot 0 = 0$

For $A = 0, B = 1$:

$Y = 0 \cdot \bar{1} = 0 \cdot 0 = 0$

Therefore, the outputs are $0$ and $0$ respectively.

Answer: $0, 0$ respectively

43757.sol:
Suppose $m$ grams of water evaporate. Then, heat required
$\Delta{Q}_{req} = m{L}_{v}$
Mass that converts into ice $= \left(150 - m\right)
Heat released$ in the process,
\Delta{Q}_{rel} = $\left(150 - m\right)${L}_{f}$
Now, $\Delta{Q}_{rel} = \Delta{Q}_{req}$
\left(150 - m\right)${L}_{f} = m{L}_{v}$
$m$\left({L}_{f} + {L}_{v}\right) = 150{L}_{f}$
$m = \dfrac{150{L}_{f}}{{L}_{f} + {L}_{v}}$
$m = 20g$

45654.subject: Chemistry
45654.text: Which amongst the following is the most stable carbocation?
45654.sol:
The most stable carbocation is $t$-alkyl carbocation because the order of stability of alkyl carbocation is $t$-alkyl $\gt s$-alkyl $\gt$ p-alkyl $\gt \mathrm{CH}_3^{+}$ carbocation. This stability order is described with the help of hyperconjugation and inductive effect. On the basis of hyper conjugation, $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}$ shows six resonating structures due to presence of six $\alpha \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds,

due to presence of nine $\alpha \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds $\stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_3$ does not show the property of resonance while $\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_2$ shows three resonating structures due to presence of three $\alpha \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds. Hence, larger number of resonating structures are possible in (2), so it is most stable. The above order of stability is also explained with the help of (+) I-effect of $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ group. More the number of $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ group. more will be tendency to displace the electrons towards positive charged carbon of carbocation. Thus (+) charge is decreased or compensated i.e, positive charge is decreased and stability of carbocation is increased.
45654.meta: Which amongst the following is the most stable carbocation?

45956.text: The ratio of the difference in energy between the first and the second Bohr orbit to that between the second and the third Bohr orbit is
45956.sol:
Energy of the \(\mathrm{n}^{\text{th }}\) Bohr's orbit is given by
\(E_n=-13.6 \times \frac{z^2}{n^2} e V\)
For H -atom, \(\mathrm{Z}=1\)
The difference in energy between the first and the second Bohr orbit:
$\begin{aligned}
& E_2-E_1=13.6 \times 1^2 \times\left(\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{2^2}\right) \\
& =13.6 \times \frac{3}{4} e V
\end{aligned}\) The $difference in energy between the second and the third Bohr orbit:\begin{aligned}
& E_3-E_2=13.6 \times 1^2 \times$\left(\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{3^2}$\right)$\\
& =13.6 \times \frac{5}{36} e V
\end{aligned}\)
Taking$ the $ratio, we get :
\(\frac{E_2-E_1}{E_3-E_2}=\frac{13.6 \times \frac{3}{4}}{13.6 \times \frac{5}{36}}=\frac{27}{5}\)$

50230.subject: Physics
50230.text: A mass M is hung with a light inextensible string as shown in figure. Find the tension of the horizontal string.
50230.sol:
Let $T_1$ be the tension in the horizontal string, $T_2$ be the tension in the slanted string, and $T_3$ be the tension in the vertical string.

For the mass $M$ in equilibrium, the tension in the vertical string is:
$T_3 = Mg$

Considering the equilibrium of the knot O, we can resolve the forces in the horizontal and vertical directions.

Balancing the forces in the vertical direction:
$T_2 \sin 45^{\circ} = T_3 = Mg$

Balancing the forces in the horizontal direction:
$T_1 = T_2 \cos 45^{\circ}$

Dividing the vertical force equation by the horizontal force equation, we get:
$\dfrac{T_2 \sin 45^{\circ}}{T_2 \cos 45^{\circ}} = \dfrac{Mg}{T_1}$

$\tan 45^{\circ} = \dfrac{Mg}{T_1}$

Since $\tan 45^{\circ} = 1$, we have:
$1 = \dfrac{Mg}{T_1}$

$T_1 = Mg$

Thus, the tension in the horizontal string is $Mg$.

Answer: $Mg$

56836.subject: Chemistry
56836.text: Which from following options is true when an electrolyte solution is diluted ?
56836.sol:
When an electrolyte solution is diluted, the volume of the solution increases, which leads to a decrease in the number of ions per unit volume. As a result, the specific conductivity (k$) decreases.

Molar conductivity (\Lambda$) is the conductance of the volume of solution containing one mole of the electrolyte. It is given by $\Lambda = k \times V$. Upon dilution, the increase in volume (V$) more than compensates for the decrease in specific conductivity (k$). Additionally, for weak electrolytes, the degree of dissociation increases, and for strong electrolytes, interionic attractions decrease, leading to higher ionic mobility. Thus, molar conductivity (\Lambda$) increases.

Therefore, \Lambda$ increases and $k$ decreases.

Answer: $\Lambda$ increases and $k$ decreases

59165.text:
Calculate vapour pressure of pure volatile liquid B at given temperature if mole faction of liquid $B$ and vapour pressure of pure volatile liquid A are 0.4 and 400 mm Hg respectively.
$\left[\mathrm{P}_{\text{toal }}=600 \mathrm{ mm} \mathrm{Hg}\right]$
59165.sol:
Vapor pressure of pure volatile liquid B

Using Raoult's law for a mixture of two volatile liquids, the total vapor pressure is $P_{\text{total}} = X_A P_A^0 + X_B P_B^0$, where $X_A$ and $X_B$ are the mole fractions, and $P_A^0$ and $P_B^0$ are the pure vapor pressures. Given $X_B = 0.4$, $P_A^0 = 400\,\text{mm Hg}$, and $P_{\text{total}} = 600\,\text{mm Hg}$, determine $X_A = 1 - X_B = 0.6$.

Substitute the known values:

$600 = (0.6)(400) + (0.4) P_B^0$

Simplify the first term:

$600 = 240 + 0.4 P_B^0$

Isolate $P_B^0$:

$0.4 P_B^0 = 360$

Solve:

$P_B^0 = \frac{360}{0.4} = 900\,\text{mm Hg}$

The vapor pressure of pure volatile liquid B is $\boxed{900\,\text{mm Hg}}$.

$\mathrm{As}_2\mathrm{S}_3, clay, and Congo Red sols are negatively charged, while haemoglobin is not.

62567.text:
The number of solutions of
$\tan ^{-1}\left(x+\frac{2}{x}\right)-\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{x}\right)-\tan ^{-1}\left(x-\frac{2}{x}\right)=0$ are
62567.sol:
The equation $\tan^{-1}\left(x+\frac{2}{x}\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{x}\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(x-\frac{2}{x}\right)=0$ simplifies by rearranging to $\tan^{-1} \left(x+\frac{2}{x}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{x}\right)+\tan^{-1}\lleft(x-\frac{2}{x}\right).$

Applying the identity $\tan^{-1} A + \tan^{-1} B = \tan^{-1} \left(\frac{A+B}{1-AB}\right)for $ AB < 1$, with $A = $\frac{4}{x}and $ B = $x-\frac{2}{x},yields $ A+B = $x+\frac{2}{x}and $ AB = $4-\frac{8}{x^2}.

Substituting gives the right-hand side as \tan^{-1} \left(\frac{x+\frac{2}{x}}{-3+\frac{8}{x^2}}\right).$ With common denominators, this becomes $\tan^{-1} \left(\frac{(x^2+2)x}{8-3x^2}\right).

Equating arguments requires x+\frac{2}{x} = \frac{(x^2+2)x}{8-3x^2},valid for $ x ≠ 0$ and 8-3x^2 ≠ 0$. Simplifying leads to $\frac{1}{x} = \frac{x}{8-3x^2}$,so $8-3x^2 = x²$, giving $x^2 = 2$ and $x = $\pm\sqrt{2}.

Both values satisfy the original equation and the condition $ AB = 0 < 1$, confirming they are valid solutions.

Final answer: $\boxed{2}$

63152.text: The inverse of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 4 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ is $B = \dfrac{1}{37}\begin{bmatrix} -5 & 9 & 11 \\ -3 & -2 & 14 \\ 11 & -5 & k \end{bmatrix}$, then the value of $k$ is...
63152.sol:
Since $B$ is the inverse of $A$, we have $AB = I$, which implies $A(37B) = 37I$.

The element in the first row and third column of the matrix $37I$ is $0$.

Multiplying the first row of $A$ with the third column of $37B$, we get:

$2(11) + (-1)(14) + 4(k) = 0$

$22 - 14 + 4k = 0$

$8 + 4k = 0$

$k = -2$

Alternatively, multiplying the third row of $A$ with the third column of $37B$ gives the element in the third row and third column of $37I$, which is $37$:

$1(11) + 2(14) + 1(k) = 37$

$11 + 28 + k = 37$

$39 + k = 37$

$k = -2$

Answer: $-2$

63647.text: If a random variable $X$ follows the Binomial distribution $B(10, p)$ such that $5 P(X=0)=P(X=1)$, then the value of $\frac{P(X=5)}{P(X=6)}$ is equal to
63647.sol:
Given $X \sim B(10, p)$ with the condition $5P(X=0) = P(X=1)$. The probability $P(X=0) = (1-p)^{10}$ and $P(X=1) = 10p(1-p)^9$.

Substituting into the given relation yields $5(1-p)^{10} = 10p(1-p)^9$. For $p \neq 1$, dividing both sides by $(1-p)^9$ gives $5(1-p) = 10p$, leading to $p = \frac{1}{3}$.

The ratio $\frac{P(X=5)}{P(X-6)}$ simplifies to $\frac{\binom{10}{5}}{\binom{10}{6}} \cdot \frac{1-p}{p}$. Using the identity $\frac{\binom{10}{5}}{\binom{10}{6}} = \frac{6}{5}$ and substituting $p = \frac{1}{3}$, $1-p = \frac{2}{3}$, we obtain:

$\frac{P(X=5)}{P(X=6)} = \frac{6}{5} \cdot \frac{2/3}{1/3} = \frac{6}{5} \cdot 2 = \frac{12}{5}$.

Final answer: $\frac{12}{5}$

64495.subject: Mathematics
64495.text: If the angle $\theta$ between the line $\frac{x+1}{1}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z-2}{2}$ and the plane $2 x-\mathrm{y}+\sqrt{\lambda} \mathrm{z}+4=0$ is such that $\sin \theta=\frac{1}{3}$, then $\lambda+1=$
64495.sol:
The angle between a line with direction vector $\vec{b}$ and a plane with normal vector $\vec{n}$ satisfies $\sin \theta = \frac{|\vec{b} \cdot \vec{n}|}{|\vec{b}| |\vec{n}|}$.

Given the line $\frac{x+1}{1} = \frac{y-1}{2} = \frac{z-2}{2}$, its direction vector is $\vec{b} = \langle 1, 2, 2 \rangle$ with magnitude $|\vec{b}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2 + 2^2} = 3$.

The plane $2x - y + \sqrt{\lambda}z + 4 = 0$ has normal vector $\vec{n} = \langle 2, -1, \sqrt{\lambda} \rangle$ and magnitude $|\vec{n}| = \sqrt{4 + 1 + \lambda} = \sqrt{5 + \lambda}$.

The dot product evaluates to $\vec{b} \cdot \vec{n} = 2 - 2 + 2\sqrt{\lambda} = 2\sqrt{\lambda}$.

Substituting $\sin \theta = \frac{1}{3}$ into the formula yields:

$\frac{1}{3} = \frac{2\sqrt{\lambda}}{3\sqrt{5 + \lambda}}$

Multiplying both sides by 3 gives $1 = \frac{2\sqrt{\lambda}}{\sqrt{5 + \lambda}}$.
Squaring both sides produces $1 = \frac{4\lambda}{5 + \lambda}$, so $5 + \lambda = 4\lambda$ and $\lambda = \frac{5}{3}$.

Thus, $\lambda + 1 = \frac{8}{3}$, confirming the answer.

\frac{16}{3R} = \frac{20}{x} \cdot \frac{36}{5R}
Cancel $R and $simplify:
\frac{16}{3} = \frac{144}{x}
Solving yields$x = 27$.

Final answer: $\boxed{27}$

70203.subject: Physics
70203.text: Four polaroids are placed such that the optic axis of each is inclined at an angle of $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the optic axis of the preceding one. If unpolarised light of intensity ' $\mathrm{I}_0$ ' falls on the first polaroid, the intensity of light transmitted from the fourth polaroid is $[\cos 30=\sqrt{3} / 2]$
70203.sol:
Unpolarized light of intensity $I_0$ passes through the first polarizer, reducing the intensity by half: $I_1 = \frac{I_0}{2}$.

The second polarizer is oriented at $30^{}^{\circ}$ to the first. Applying Malus's Law: $I_2 = I_1 \cos^2 30^{}^{\circ} = \frac{I_0}{2} \cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{3I_0}{8}$.

Each subsequent polarizer is rotated an additional $30^{}^{\circ}$ from the previous one, multiplying by $\cos^2 30^{}^{\circ} = \frac{3}{4}$ each time.

After three such rotations: $I_4 = \frac{I_0}{2} \cdot \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^3 = \frac{27I_0}{128}$.

The final intensity is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

70412.subject: Physics
70412.text: A set of $14$ tuning forks is arranged in a series of increasing frequencies. Each fork produces '$x$' beats per second with the preceding fork and the last fork is an octave of the first fork. If the seventh fork has the frequency of $114$ Hz, the value of $x$ is
70412.sol:
Let the frequency of the first tuning fork be $f_1$.

Since each fork produces $x$ beats per second with the preceding fork and the frequencies are in increasing order, the frequencies form an arithmetic progression with a common difference of $x$.

The frequency of the $n$-th tuning fork is given by $f_n = f_1 + (n - 1)x$.

The frequency of the 14th tuning fork is $f_{14} = f_1 + 13x$.

It is given that the last fork is an octave of the first fork, which means $f_{14} = 2f_1$.

Substituting this into the equation, we get $2f_1 = f_1 + 13x \Rightarrow f_1 = 13x$.

The frequency of the 7th tuning fork is given as $114$ Hz.

Using the formula for the 7th fork, $f_7 = f_1 + 6x$.

Substituting $f_1 = 13x$, we get $f_7 = 13x + 6x = 19x$.

Equating this to the given frequency, $19x = 114$.

Solving for $x$, we get $x = \dfrac{114}{19} = 6$.

Answer: $6$

70960.subject: Biology
70960.text: The organic compounds that are tightly attached to the protein part of an enzyme to make them catalatically active are called -------------------.
70960.sol:
According to NCERT Biology, cofactors are non-protein constituents bound to the enzyme to make it catalytically active.

There are three kinds of cofactors: prosthetic groups, co-enzymes, and metal ions.

Prosthetic groups are organic compounds that are distinguished from other cofactors in that they are tightly bound to the apoenzyme (the protein part of the enzyme).

Co-enzymes are also organic compounds, but their association with the apoenzyme is only transient.

Therefore, the organic compounds tightly attached to the protein part of an enzyme are called prosthetic groups.

Answer: prosthetic groups

71666.subject: Chemistry
71666.text: Which of the following reagents is used to identify one primary alcoholic group of glucose?
71666.sol:
Glucose contains one primary alcoholic group at the C-6 position.

When glucose is treated with dilute $\text{HNO}_3$, both the terminal aldehyde group and the primary alcoholic group are oxidized to carboxylic acid groups, resulting in the formation of saccharic acid (glucaric acid).

This specific oxidation reaction confirms the presence of a primary alcoholic group in glucose.

$\text{Br}_2$ water is a mild oxidizing agent that oxidizes only the aldehyde group to form gluconic acid, confirming the presence of an aldehyde group.

Acetic anhydride forms glucose pentaacetate, confirming the presence of five hydroxyl groups.

$\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$ forms an oxime, confirming the presence of a carbonyl group.

Answer: dilute $\text{HNO}_3$

71785.subject: Chemistry
71785.text: The molar conductance of NaCl, HCl and $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ at infinite dilution are 126.45, 426.16 and 91.0 S $\text{cm}^2\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. Calculate the molar conductance of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ at infinite dilution?
71785.sol:
According to Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions:

$\Lambda^{}^{\circ}_m(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}) = \Lambda^{}^{\circ}_m(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}) + \Lambda^{}^{\circ}_m(\text{HCl}) - \Lambda^{}^{\circ}_m(\text{NaCl})$

Substituting the given values:

$\Lambda^{}^{\circ}_m(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}) = 91.0 + 426.16 - 126.45$

$\Lambda^{}^{\circ}_m(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}) = 517.16 - 126.45 = 390.71 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: 390.71 S $\text{cm}^2\ \text{mol}^{-1}$

72022.subject: Chemistry
72022.text: Calculate the energy associated with an electron in the first orbit of hydrogen atom?
72022.sol:
The energy of an electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit of a hydrogen-like species is given by the Bohr model as:

$E_n = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}\ \text{J}$

For a hydrogen atom, the atomic number $Z = 1$.

For the first orbit, the principal quantum number $n = 1$.

Substituting these values into the formula, we get:

$E_1 = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \dfrac{1^2}{1^2}\ \text{J}$

$E_1 = -2.18 \times 10^{-18}\ \text{J}$

Answer: $-2.18 \times 10^{-18}\ \text{J}$

72207.subject: Physics
72207.text: Three electric charges $2q$, $2q$, $-4q$ are placed at the corners of equilateral triangle of side $'x'$. The magnitude of electric dipole moment of the system is
72207.sol:
The system of charges can be considered as two dipoles by splitting the $-4q$ charge into two charges of $-2q$ each.

One dipole is formed by $-2q$ and $2q$ along one side of the equilateral triangle, having a dipole moment $p_1 = (2q)x = 2qx$.

The second dipole is formed by the other $-2q$ and $2q$ along the adjacent side, having a dipole moment $p_2 = (2q)x = 2qx$.

The angle between the two dipole moment vectors is $60^{{}^{\circ}}$, which is the interior angle of the equilateral triangle.

The magnitude of the resultant dipole moment is given by:

$p_{net} = \sqrt{p_1^2 + p_2^2 + 2p_1p_2\cos 60^{{}^{\circ}}}$

Substituting $p_1 = p_2 = 2qx$ and $\cos 60^{{}^{\circ}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$:

$p_{net} = \sqrt{(2qx)^2 + (2qx)^2 + 2(2qx)(2qx)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}$

$p_{net} = \sqrt{4q^2x^2 + 4q^2x^2 + 4q^2x^2}$

$p_{net} = \sqrt{12q^2x^2} = 2\sqrt{3}qx$

Answer: $2\sqrt{3}qx$

72425.text: One mole of an ideal gas in initial state A undergoes a cyclic process ABCA, as shown in the figure. Its pressure at A is $P_0$. Choose the correct option from the following.
options: Internal energies at A and B are not the same.
Work done by the gas in process AB is $P_0 V_0\ln(4)$
72425.sol:
From the given $V-T$ graph, the parameters for states A and B are:
State A: $T_A = T_0$, $V_A = V_0$, $P_A = P_0$
State B: $T_B = T_0$, $V_B = 4V_0$

Since $T_A = T_B = T_0$, the process AB is isothermal. For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature, which means $U_A = U_B$.

The work done by the gas in the isothermal process AB is:
$W_{AB} = nRT_0 \ln \left(\dfrac{V_B}{V_A}\right)

Given $n = 1$ mole, and using the ideal gas equation at state A ($P_0 V_0 = RT_0$), we get:
$W_{AB} = P_0 V_0 \ln$\left(\dfrac{4V_0}{V_0}\right) =$ P_0 V_0 \ln(4)$

The line BC is straight but not specified to pass through the origin. If it did, both $P_C = $\dfrac{P_0}{4}$ and T_C = $\dfrac{T_0}{4} would be true, leading$ to multiple correct options. Thus, only the work done in process AB is definitively correct.

Answer: Work done by the gas in process AB is P_0 V_0\ln(4)

73871.subject: General Ability
73871.text: Which one of the following statements for the work done by gravity on a body is NOT correct?
options: Work done is independent of the path followed by the body
Work done depends only on the vertical distance separating the initial and the final position of the body
Work done depends on the path followed by the body
Work done is zero if the body is displaced horizontally to the force of gravity
73871.sol:
The gravitational force is a conservative force.

For any conservative force, the work done is independent of the path taken and depends only on the initial and final positions of the body.

Specifically for gravity, the work done is given by $W = mgh$, where $h$ is the vertical displacement. Thus, it depends only on the vertical distance separating the initial and final positions.

If the displacement is purely horizontal, the angle between the gravitational force (downwards) and the displacement is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$. The work done is $W = Fd \cos(90^{{}^{\circ}}) = 0$.

Therefore, the statement that work done depends on the path followed by the body is incorrect.

Answer: Work done depends on the path followed by the body

75088.subject: General Ability
75088.text:
Consider the following statements about temperature inversion:
I. This happens when normal lapse rate gets inverted.
II. Winter nights with cloudy skies are conducive for temperature inversion.
III. Polar areas experience inversion throughout the year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75088.sol:
Temperature inversion is a reversal of the normal behavior of temperature in the troposphere, where a layer of cool air at the surface is overlain by a layer of warmer air. Under normal conditions, temperature usually decreases with height, which is known as the normal lapse rate. When this is reversed, the normal lapse rate gets inverted. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Ideal conditions for temperature inversion include long winter nights, clear skies, calm air, and dry air. Cloudy skies prevent the rapid cooling of the earth's surface by trapping outgoing terrestrial radiation, which hinders the formation of a temperature inversion. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

In polar regions, due to the extremely cold surface, temperature inversion is a normal phenomenon that occurs throughout the year. Thus, Statement III is correct.

Therefore, only statements I and III are correct.

Answer: I and III only

77027.subject: Mathematics
77027.text: $What is the degree of the differential equation \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}} = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{\frac{5}{2}}$?
77027.sol:
The given differential equation is $\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\dfrac{3}{2}} = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{\dfrac{5}{2}}$.

To find the degree of the differential equation, the powers of the derivatives must be made integers. Squaring both sides, we get:

$\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^3 = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^5$

The highest order derivative is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$, which has an order of $2$.

The power of the highest order derivative is $3$.

Therefore, the degree of the differential equation is $3$.

77490.subject: Mathematics
77490.text:
Let $\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c$
What is the value of $\alpha$ ?
77490.sol:
Given,
$\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c\qquad....(i)$
Let, $\quad \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}\begin{aligned}
& =\int \frac{(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1}) d x}{(\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1})(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1})} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{(x+1)} d x+\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{x-1} d x \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+\frac{\frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \ldots(ii)
\end{aligned}$
From (i) and (ii) we get
$\alpha=\frac{1}{3}$

83600.text: A deep rectangular pond of surface area $\mathrm{A}$, containing water (density $=\rho$, specific heat capacity $=s$ ), is located in a region where the outside air temperature is a steady value at the $-26^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Key Idea If area of cross-section of a surface is not uniform or if the steady state condition is not reached, the heat flow equation can be applied to a thin layer of material perpendicular to direction of heat flow.
The rate of heat flow by conduction for growth of ice is given by,

$\frac{d \theta}{d t}=\frac{\left.K A\left(\theta_0-\theta_0\right)\right]}{x}$where, $d \theta=\rho A d x L, \theta_0=0$ and $\theta_1=-\theta$
Given, $\theta_0=0^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}, \theta_1=-26^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$
The rate of increase of thickness can be calculated from Eq.

$\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}$& =$\frac{\mathrm{KA}\left(\theta_0-\theta_1\right)}{\mathrm{x}}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{\rho \mathrm{AdxL}}{\mathrm{dt}}$& =$\frac{\mathrm{KA}\left(\theta_0-\theta_1\right)}{\mathrm{x}}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}$& =$\frac{\mathrm{KA}\left(\theta_0-\theta_1\right)}{\rho \mathrm{AxL}}$\\
& =$\frac{\mathrm{K}[0-(-26)]}{\rho \times \mathrm{L}}=\frac{26 \mathrm{~K}}{\rho \times \mathrm{L}}
\end{aligned}$

84704.subject: Zoology
84704.text:
Choose the correct statements regarding muscle contraction.
A. A motor neuron carries a signal sent by the Central Nervous System (CNS) to the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre.
B. The neural signal generates an action potential which causes the release of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ into sarcoplasm.
C. Increase in $\text{Ca}^{++}$ inactivates the actin for breaking cross bridges.
D. Actin binds to the myosin head to form a cross bridge.
E. Shortening of sarcomere takes place, by pulling actin filaments towards the centre of 'A' band.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A, B, D and E only
84704.sol:
Statement A is correct: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the Central Nervous System (CNS) via a motor neuron to the neuromuscular junction, which is the junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre.

Statement B is correct: The neural signal releases a neurotransmitter (acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma. This action potential spreads through the muscle fibre and causes the release of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ ions into the sarcoplasm.

Statement C is incorrect: An increase in $\text{Ca}^{++}$ level leads to the binding of calcium with a subunit of troponin on actin filaments, which removes the masking of active sites for myosin. It does not inactivate actin.

Statement D is correct: Utilising the energy from ATP hydrolysis, the myosin head binds to the exposed active sites on actin to form a cross bridge.

Statement E is correct: The formation of cross bridges pulls the attached actin filaments towards the centre of the 'A' band. The 'Z' lines attached to these actins are also pulled inwards, causing a shortening of the sarcomere, which is muscle contraction.

Therefore, statements A, B, D, and E are correct.

Answer: A, B, D and E only

options: polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually.
polyps produce medusae sexually and medusae form the polyps asexually.
both polyps and medusae are produced sexually by each other.
both polyps and medusae are produced asexually by each other.
95597.sol: Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa. The former is a sessile and cylindrical form like Hydra, Adamsia, etc. whereas, the latter is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming like Aurelia or jellyfish. Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (Metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g., Obelia).

100339.subject: Physics
100339.text:
An observer moves at a constant speed $v_0$ parallel to a regular service of buses. The buses operate in both directions at a constant speed $v_b$ (where $v_b > v_0$) with a departure time period $T$. Consider the following statements:

A. The spatial distance between two consecutive buses moving in the same direction is $(v_b - v_0)T$.
B. The time interval between the observer's encounters with buses moving in the opposite direction is strictly less than $T$.
C. If the observer's speed $v_0$ increases, the time interval between encounters with buses moving in the same direction also increases.
D. The relative speed of buses moving in one direction with respect to buses moving in the opposite direction is zero.

How many of the above statements are correct?
100339.sol:
Statement A is incorrect: The spatial distance between consecutive buses depends only on the bus speed and departure period, given by $d = v_b T$, which is independent of the observer's speed.

Statement B is correct: The time interval for opposite direction encounters is $t_{\text{opp}} = \dfrac{d}{v_b + v_0} = \dfrac{v_b T}{v_b + v_0}$. Since $v_b + v_0 > v_b$, it follows that $t_{\text{opp}} < T$.

Statement C is correct: The time interval for same direction encounters is $t_{\text{same}} = \dfrac{d}{v_b - v_0} = \dfrac{v_b T}{v_b - v_0}$. As $v_0$ increases, the denominator $(v_b - v_0)$ decreases, causing $t_{\text{same}}$ to increase.

Statement D is incorrect: The relative speed between buses moving in opposite directions is $v_b - (-v_b) = 2v_b$, not zero.

Therefore, exactly two statements (B and C) are correct.

Answer: Only two

101083.text: A toy truck of mass 2 m elastically collides with a toy car of mass $m$. speed of truck is $v$ and car is at rest. Find the velocity of car after collision.
101083.sol:
Mass of toy truck $m_t=2 \mathrm{~m}$
Mass of toy car $\mathrm{m}_c=\mathrm{m}$
Initial speed of truck $v_t=v$
and initial speed of car $u_c=0$
If $v_1 and v_2$ be the final velocity of truck and car after collision, then by law of conservation of momentum,
Total initial momentum $=$ total final momentum
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{t}} \cdot \mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{t}}+\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{c}} \mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{c}} & =\mathrm{m}_4 \mathrm{v}_1+\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{c}} \mathrm{v}_2 \\
2 \mathrm{mv}+0 & =2 \mathrm{mv}_1+\mathrm{mv}_2 \\
2 \mathrm{v} & =2 \mathrm{v}_1+\mathrm{v}_2
\end{aligned}$
For elastic collision, coefficient of restitution, $e=1$
i.e.
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{v_2-v_1}{u_1-u_c}=1 \\
& \frac{v_2-v_1}{v-0}=1 \Rightarrow v=v_2-v_1
\end{aligned}$
Solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we have $\mathrm{v}_2=\frac{4 \mathrm{v}}{3}$

103698.subject: Physics
103698.text: A thin, straight bar magnet of length $L$ has a magnetic moment $M$. If it is bent into a complete semicircle, what will be its new magnetic moment?
103698.sol:
The initial magnetic moment of the straight bar magnet is given by $M = m \times L$, where $m$ is the pole strength and $L$ is the length of the magnet.

When the magnet is bent into a complete semicircle, its length $L$ becomes the circumference of the semicircle. If $R$ is the radius of this semicircle, then:
$\pi R = L \Rightarrow R = \dfrac{L}{\pi}$

The new effective length of the magnet is the shortest straight-line distance between its two poles, which is the diameter of the semicircle:
$L' = 2R = \dfrac{2L}{\pi}$

The pole strength $m$ remains unchanged. Therefore, the new magnetic moment $M'$ is:
$M' = m \times L' = m \times \left(\dfrac{2L}{\pi}\right) = \dfrac{2(m \times L)}{\pi} = \dfrac{2M}{\pi}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2M}{\pi}$

$\text{O}_2$ (16 electrons): The molecular orbital configuration is $\sigma_{1s}^2 \ {\sigma^{*}}_{1s}^2 \ \sigma_{2s}^2 \ {\sigma^{*}}_{2s}^2 \ \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \ \pi_{2p_x}^2 = \pi_{2p_y}^2 \ {\pi^{*}}_{2p_x}^1 = {\pi^{*}}_{2p_y}^1$. The HOMO is $\pi^{*}_{2p}$.

$\text{Ne}_2$ (20 electrons): The molecular orbital configuration is $\sigma_{1s}^2 \ {\sigma^{*}}_{1s}^2 \ \sigma_{2s}^2 \ {\sigma^{*}}_{2s}^2 \ \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \ \pi_{2p_x}^2 = \pi_{2p_y}^2 \ {\pi^{*}}_{2p_x}^2 = {\pi^{*}}_{2p_y}^2 \ {\sigma^{*}}_{2p_z}^2$. The HOMO is $\sigma^{*}_{2p_z}$.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)

113935.subject: Chemistry
113935.text: The variation of total vapour pressure ($P$) of an ideal solution of two volatile liquids P and Q with the mole fraction of component P ($X_P$) is a straight line. The line has a y-intercept of $150\text{ torr}$ at $X_P = 0$ and a y-intercept of $250\text{ torr}$ at $X_P = 1$. If a solution is prepared by mixing P and Q in a $3 : 2$ molar ratio, what is the total vapour pressure of this mixture?
113935.sol:
From the given boundary conditions of the graph:
At $X_P = 0$, the solution contains only liquid Q. Thus, the vapour pressure of pure Q is $P_Q^{\circ} = 150\text{ torr}$.
At $X_P = 1$, the solution contains only liquid P. Thus, the vapour pressure of pure P is $P_P^{\circ} = 250\text{ torr}$.

The liquids P and Q are mixed in a molar ratio of $3 : 2$.
Mole fraction of P, $X_P = \dfrac{3}{3 + 2} = \dfrac{3}{5} = 0.6$
Mole fraction of Q, $X_Q = \dfrac{2}{3 + 2} = \dfrac{2}{5} = 0.4$

According to Raoult's law, the total vapour pressure is:
$P_{\text{total}} = X_P P_P^{\circ} + X_Q P_Q^{\circ}$
$P_{\text{total}} = (0.6 \times 250) + (0.4 \times 150)$
$P_{\text{total}} = 150 + 60 = 210\text{ torr}$

Answer: $210\text{ torr}$

114360.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For the concentration cell $Pt | H_2(1 \text{ bar}) | H^+(pH=3) || H^+(pH=2) | H_2(1 \text{ bar}) | Pt$, the cell potential is positive.
Reason (R): In a concentration cell, the cell potential is positive if the concentration of the active ion in the cathodic half-cell is greater than that in the anodic half-cell.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
114360.sol:
For a hydrogen concentration cell, the net cell reaction is:
$H^+(\text{cathode}) \rightarrow H^+(\text{anode})$

Using the Nernst equation at $298 \text{ K}$:
$E_{cell} = E^\circ_{cell} - \dfrac{0.059}{1} \log \dfrac{[H^+]_{\text{anode}}}{[H^+]_{\text{cathode}}}$

Since $E^\circ_{cell} = 0$ for a concentration cell, $E_{cell}$ will be positive only if $\log \dfrac{[H^+]_{\text{anode}}}{[H^+]_{\text{cathode}}} < 0$, which means $[H^+]_{\text{cathode}} > [H^+]_{\text{anode}}$. Thus, Reason (R) is correct.

Evaluating Assertion (A):
At the anode, $pH = 3 \implies [H^+]_{\text{anode}} = 10^{-3} \text{ M}$
At the cathode, $pH = 2 \implies [H^+]_{\text{cathode}} = 10^{-2} \text{ M}$

Since $[H^+]_{\text{cathode}} > [H^+]_{\text{anode}}$, the cell potential $E_{cell}$ is positive. Therefore, Assertion (A) is correct.

Reason (R) correctly explains why the cell potential in Assertion (A) is positive.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

118793.subject: Chemistry
118793.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Chlorobenzene cannot be converted to phenol by boiling with aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ at standard temperature and pressure.
Reason (R): In chlorobenzene, the $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond acquires a partial double bond character due to resonance, making it difficult to cleave.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
118793.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct. Aryl halides like chlorobenzene are extremely less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reactions under normal conditions. The conversion of chlorobenzene to phenol (Dow's process) requires drastic conditions: $623\text{ K}$ temperature and $300\text{ atm}$ pressure.

Reason (R) is also correct and explains the Assertion. In chlorobenzene, the lone pair of electrons on the chlorine atom is in conjugation with the pi-electrons of the benzene ring. This resonance imparts a partial double bond character to the $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond. As a result, the bond cleavage in chlorobenzene is much more difficult than in alkyl halides, rendering it unreactive towards aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ at standard temperature and pressure.

Hence, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

121221.subject: Botany
121221.text:
Read the following statements regarding the universal rules of nomenclature:

A. Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics.
B. The first word in a biological name represents the specific epithet.
C. Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined.
D. The specific epithet starts with a capital letter.

How many of the above statements are correct?
121221.sol:
Let us evaluate each statement based on the universal rules of nomenclature.

Statement A is correct: Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics.

Statement B is incorrect: The first word in a biological name represents the genus, while the second component denotes the specific epithet.

Statement C is correct: Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined to indicate their Latin origin.

Statement D is incorrect: The specific epithet starts with a small letter, whereas the genus starts with a capital letter.

Thus, exactly two statements (A and C) are correct.

Answer: Two

123709.sol: The nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear, cytokinesis follows and this is called as dyad of cells. 125842.text: How can pollen grains be stored for years?

125842.sol: When once they are shed, pollen grains have to land on the stigma before they lose viability if they have to bring about fertilisation. How long do you think the pollen grains retain viability? The period for which pollen grains remain viable is highly variable and to some extent depends on the prevailing temperature and humidity. In some cereals such as rice and wheat, pollen grains lose viability within 30 minutes of their release, and in some members of Rosaceae, Leguminoseae and Solanaceae, they maintain viability for months. You may have heard of storing semen/ sperms of many animals including humans for artificial insemination. It is possible to store pollen grains of a large number of species for years in liquid nitrogen (-1960C). Related Theory
The main functions of the myelin sheath in neuron are:
(I) It acts as an electrical insulator for the neuron.
(2) The sheath prevents the movement of ions into or out of the neuron, thus preventing depolarisation.
(3) It speeds up transmission of an electrical impulse in the neuron - impulses cannot travel through the sheath (the sheath acts as an electrical insulator), instead, impulses 'jump' from a gap in the myelin sheath to another gap (it jumps from one Node of Ranvier to another Node). 129704.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The continuous flow of blood through the vasa recta washes away the dissolved solutes from the medullary interstitium, thereby destroying the concentration gradient.

Reason (R): Blood flows in opposite directions in the descending and ascending limbs of the vasa recta, and NaCl is returned to the interstitium by its ascending portion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
129704.sol:
Assertion (A) is false because the vasa recta actually helps in maintaining the medullary interstitial gradient rather than washing it away. It acts as a counter-current exchanger.

Reason (R) is true. The counter-current flow of blood within the U-shaped vasa recta ensures that NaCl picked up by the descending limb is returned to the interstitium by the ascending limb, which prevents the washout of the concentration gradient.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

129785.subject: Zoology
129785.text: How do sponges exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide?
options: Through simple diffusion over their entire body surface
129785.sol: Mechanisms of breathing vary among different groups of animals depending mainly on their habitats and levels of organisation. Lower invertebrates like sponges, coelenterates, flatworms, etc., exchange O2 with CO2 by simple diffusion over their entire body surface. Earthworms use their moist cuticle and insects have a network of tubes (tracheal tubes) to transport atmospheric air within the body. Special vascularized structures called gills (branchial respiration) are used by most of the aquatic arthropods and molluscs whereas vascularised bags called lungs (pulmonary respiration) are used by the terrestrial forms for the exchange of gases. Among vertebrates, fishes use gills whereas amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals respire through lungs. Amphibians like frogs can respire through their moist skin (cutaneous respiration) also.

134138.subject: Zoology
134138.text: What is the main advantage of using PCR in diagnosing diseases?
134138.sol: You know that for effective treatment of a disease, early diagnosis and understanding its pathophysiology is very important. Using conventional methods of diagnosis (serum and urine analysis, etc.) early detection is not possible. Recombinant DNA technology, Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) and Enzyme Linked Immuno-sorbent Assay (ELISA) are some of the techniques that serve the purpose of early diagnosis. Presence of a pathogen (bacteria, viruses, etc.) is normally suspected only when the pathogen has produced a disease symptom. By this time the concentration of pathogen is already very high in the body. However, very low concentration of a bacteria or virus (at a time when the symptoms of the disease are not yet visible) can be detected by amplification of their nucleic acid by PCR. Can you explain how PCR can detect very low amounts of DNA? PCR is now routinely used to detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients. It is being used to detect mutations in genes in suspected cancer patients too. It is a powerful techqnique to identify many other genetic disorders. A single stranded DNA or RNA, tagged with a radioactive molecule (probe) is allowed to hybridise to its complementary DNA in a clone of cells followed by detection using autoradiography. The clone having the mutated gene will hence not appear on the photographic film, because the probe will not have complementarity with the mutated gene. ELISA is based on the principle of antigen-antibody interaction. Infection by pathogen can be detected by the presence of antigens (proteins, glycoproteins, etc.) or by detecting the antibodies synthesized against the pathogen.
134138.meta: What is the main advantage of using PCR in diagnosing diseases?

134178.subject: Zoology
options: To understand how genes contribute to the development of a disease
134178.sol: Normal physiology and development: Transgenic animals can be specifically designed to allow the study of how genes are regulated, and how they affect the normal functions of the body and its development, e.g., study of complex factors involved in growth such as insulin-like growth factor. By introducing genes from other species that alter the formation of this factor and studying the biological effects that result, information is obtained about the biological role of the factor in the body. (ii) Study of disease: Many transgenic animals are designed to increase our understanding of how genes contribute to the development of disease. These are specially made to serve as models for human diseases so that investigation of new treatments for diseases is made possible. Today transgenic models exist for many human diseases such as cancer, cystic fibrosis, rheumatoid arthritis and Alzheimer’s.

134302.subject: Zoology
134302.text:
Read the following statements regarding the mechanism of action of Bt toxin and arrange them in the correct chronological order:
A. Creation of pores in the midgut epithelial cells
B. Ingestion of inactive protoxin by the insect
C. Swelling and lysis of cells leading to death
D. Binding of active toxin to the surface of midgut epithelial cells
E. Solubilisation of protein crystals by alkaline pH

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
134302.sol:
The correct chronological sequence of events for the action of Bt toxin is as follows.

First, the insect ingests the inactive toxin or protoxin (Statement B).

Next, in the insect gut, the alkaline pH solubilises the protein crystals, converting the inactive protoxin into an active form (Statement E).

The activated toxin then binds to the surface of the midgut epithelial cells (Statement D).

This binding creates pores in the epithelial cells (Statement A).

Finally, the pores cause cell swelling and lysis, eventually leading to the death of the insect (Statement C).

Therefore, the correct order is B $\rightarrow$ E $\rightarrow$ D $\rightarrow$ A $\rightarrow$ C.

Answer: B $\rightarrow$ E $\rightarrow$ D $\rightarrow$ A $\rightarrow$ C

134873.subject: Zoology
134873.text: Agrobacterium tumefaciens, a pathogen of several dicot plants, is able to deliver a piece of DNA known as 'T-DNA' to transform normal plant cells into a tumor. What specific modification is made to its naturally occurring Ti plasmid so that it can be used as a cloning vector for plants?
options: The entire T-DNA region is deleted to prevent the formation of tumors in the host plant.
An animal origin of replication is added to allow its multiplication in a wider range of hosts.
Ampicillin resistance genes are introduced to facilitate the infection of plant cells.
The tumor-causing genes are removed, but the plasmid retains its mechanism to deliver the DNA of interest.
134873.sol:
The tumor inducing (Ti) plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens has been modified into a cloning vector which is no more pathogenic to the plants but is still able to use the mechanisms to deliver genes of our interest into a variety of plants.

This is achieved by 'disarming' the plasmid, which involves removing the pathogenic (tumor-causing) genes from the T-DNA region while retaining the sequences necessary for the transfer of DNA into the plant cell.

Deleting the entire T-DNA region would destroy its ability to transfer DNA. Adding an animal origin of replication or ampicillin resistance does not relate to its primary modification for use as a plant vector.

Answer: The tumor-causing genes are removed, but the plasmid retains its mechanism to deliver the DNA of interest.

135118.subject: Zoology
135118.text: What role do predators play in controlling prey populations?
options: They have no effect on prey populations
135118.sol: Although animals eating plants are categorized separately as herbivores, they are, in a broad ecological context, not very different from predators. <mark>Besides acting as ‘conduits’ for energy transfer across trophic levels, predators play other important roles. They keep prey populations under control. But for predators, prey species could achieve very high population densities and cause ecosystem instability</mark>. When certain exotic species are introduced into a geographical area, they become invasive and start spreading fast because the invaded land does not have its natural predators.The prickly pear cactus introduced into Australia in the early 1920’s caused havoc by spreading rapidly into millions of hectares of rangeland. Finally, the invasive cactus was brought under control only after a cactus-feeding predator (a moth) from its natural habitat was introduced into the country
135118.meta: What role do predators play in controlling prey populations?

135122.subject: Zoology
135122.text: What effect do predators have on species diversity in a community?
options: They have no effect on species diversity
135122.sol: The prickly pear cactus introduced into Australia in the early 1920’s caused havoc by spreading rapidly into millions of hectares of rangeland. Finally, the invasive cactus was brought under control only after a cactus-feeding predator (a moth) from its natural habitat was introduced into the country. Biological control methods adopted in agricultural pest control are based on the ability of the predator to regulate prey population. <mark>Predators also help in maintaining species diversity in a community, by reducing the intensity of competition among competing prey species</mark>. In the rocky intertidal communities of the American Pacific Coast the starfish Pisaster is an important predator. In a field experiment, when all the starfish were removed from an enclosed intertidal area, more than 10 species of invertebrates became extinct within a year, because of interspecific competition.
